::: {.callout-important}
## 本节考纲要求

本页依据 9709 Mathematics 2026–2027 syllabus 1.1 Quadratics：

- 对 (ax^2+bx+c) completing the square，并使用 completed-square form；
- 求 quadratic polynomial 的 discriminant，并判断 real roots、distinct roots 或 repeated root；
- 解 quadratic equations 与 quadratic inequalities；
- 用 substitution 解一个 linear equation 与一个 quadratic equation 组成的 simultaneous equations；
- 识别并解在某个 function of (x) 中为 quadratic 的方程。

下列 20 组题目均来自工作区保存的 Paper 1 原始 past-paper PDF。题干只把 PDF 排版符号整理为 LaTeX，没有改写题目或补造题目；答案按对应 mark scheme 的得分步骤展开。
:::

## 1. Core knowledge

::: {.study-card}
### Completing the square

对 (ax^2+bx+c)，先提出 (a)：

$$
ax^2+bx+c=a\left(x^2+\frac ba x\right)+c
=a\left(x+\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2+c-\frac{b^2}{4a}.
$$

因此顶点为

$$
\left(-\frac{b}{2a},\ c-\frac{b^2}{4a}\right).
$$

当 (a>0) 时是 minimum；当 (a<0) 时是 maximum。写出平方形式后，最值和 range 通常可以直接读出。
:::

::: {.worked-example}
<span class="we-tag">Worked example · 原始笔记单卡片</span>

![Completing the square in a quadratic model](../assets/notes/algebra-functions/worked-example-47.webp){.note-figure fig-alt="Original extracted worked example showing completing the square for a quadratic model"}

这张笔记例题连接本节的 completing the square、vertex 和 maximum value：先把二次式写成 (-a(x-b)^2+c)，再由平方项的符号判断最大值。
:::

::: {.formula-panel}
### Discriminant

对

$$ax^2+bx+c=0,$$

定义

$$\Delta=b^2-4ac.$$

当 (a,b,c\in\mathbb R) 时：

$$
\Delta>0\Rightarrow\text{two distinct real roots},\qquad
\Delta=0\Rightarrow\text{one repeated real root},\qquad
\Delta<0\Rightarrow\text{no real roots}.
$$

若题目问 line 与 quadratic curve 有 two distinct intersections，先令两条曲线的 (y) 相等，整理成关于 (x) 的 quadratic，再使用 (Delta>0)。问 tangent 则使用 (Delta=0)。
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Solving equations and inequalities

Quadratic equation 可以 factorise、complete the square 或使用 quadratic formula。Quadratic inequality 要先找 roots，再用 leading coefficient 判断区间符号；如果题目给出 parameter，边界通常来自 (Delta=0)。

对于 simultaneous equations，若一个方程是 linear，先将它写成 (y=\cdots) 或 (x=\cdots)，代入另一个 equation，得到一个 quadratic；解出后必须代回 linear equation 求另一变量。

若方程在 (x^3)、(x^2)、((2x-3)^2) 等整体中呈二次形式，令该整体为 (u)，先解 (u) 的 quadratic，再回代并检查原变量的定义域。
:::

## 2. Verified Paper 1 past-paper questions

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q01}
### Question 1 · 9709/13/M/J/20 Q1

Find the set of values of (m) for which the line with equation (y=mx+1) and the curve with equation

$$y=3x^2+2x+4$$

intersect at two distinct points. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

At an intersection,

$$3x^2+2x+4=mx+1,$$

so

$$3x^2+(2-m)x+3=0.$$

For two distinct intersection points, this quadratic must have two distinct real roots:

$$
(2-m)^2-4(3)(3)>0.
$$

Hence

$$
(2-m)^2>36
\Longleftrightarrow |2-m|>6.
$$

Therefore

$$\boxed{m<-4\text{ or }m>8}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q01"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-13.pdf`, Q1, and matching `9709-s20-ms-13.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q02}
### Question 2 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q6(a–b)

The equation of a curve is (y=2x^2+kx+k-1), where (k) is a constant.

(a) Given that the line (y=2x+3) is a tangent to the curve, find the value of (k). **[3]**

It is now given that (k=2).

(b) Express the equation of the curve in the form (y=2(x+a)^2+b), where (a) and (b) are constants, and hence state the coordinates of the vertex of the curve. **[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a) At an intersection,

$$2x^2+kx+k-1=2x+3,$$

so

$$2x^2+(k-2)x+(k-4)=0.
$$

Tangency means a repeated root, so the discriminant is zero:

$$
(k-2)^2-4(2)(k-4)=0.
$$

Thus

$$k^2-12k+36=(k-6)^2=0,
$$

and (oxed{k=6}).

(b) When (k=2),

$$y=2x^2+2x+1=2\left(x^2+x+\frac14\right)=2\left(x+\frac12\right)^2.$$

Therefore (a=\frac12), (b=0), and the vertex is

$$\boxed{\left(-\frac12,0\right)}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q02"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf`, Q6(a–b), and matching `9709-s20-ms-12.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q03}
### Question 3 · 9709/13/O/N/20 Q1(a–b)

(a) Express (x^2+6x+5) in the form ((x+a)^2+b), where (a) and (b) are constants. **[2]**

(b) The curve with equation (y=x^2) is transformed to the curve with equation (y=x^2+6x+5). Describe fully the transformation(s) involved. **[2]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

$$
x^2+6x+5=x^2+6x+9-4=(x+3)^2-4.
$$

So (a=3), (b=-4). The graph of (y=x^2) is translated 3 units to the left and 4 units down:

$$\boxed{\text{translation by }\begin{pmatrix}-3\\-4\end{pmatrix}}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q03"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_13.pdf`, Q1(a–b), and matching `9709_w20_ms_13.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q04}
### Question 4 · 9709/12/O/N/20 Q3

The equation of a curve is (y=2x^2+m(2x+1)), where (m) is a constant, and the equation of a line is (y=6x+4).

Show that, for all values of (m), the line intersects the curve at two distinct points. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Equating the two expressions for (y),

$$2x^2+m(2x+1)=6x+4,$$

which gives

$$2x^2+(2m-6)x+(m-4)=0.$$

Its discriminant is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta&=(2m-6)^2-4(2)(m-4)\\
&=4m^2-32m+68\\
&=4\bigl((m-4)^2+1\bigr).
\end{aligned}
$$

Since ((m-4)^2+1>0) for every real (m), (Delta>0) for every real (m). Hence the quadratic has two distinct real roots, so the line intersects the curve at two distinct points for all (m).
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q04"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_12.pdf`, Q3, and matching `9709_w20_ms_12.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q05}
### Question 5 · 9709/12/F/M/21 Q2

By using a suitable substitution, solve the equation

$$
(2x-3)^2-\frac{4}{(2x-3)^2}-3=0.
$$

**[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Let

$$u=(2x-3)^2.$$

Then (u>0), and the equation becomes

$$u-\frac4u-3=0.$$

Multiplying by (u),

$$u^2-3u-4=0=(u-4)(u+1).$$

Because (u>0), reject (u=-1), so (u=4). Therefore

$$
(2x-3)^2=4
\Longrightarrow 2x-3=\pm2.
$$

Hence

$$\boxed{x=\frac12\text{ or }x=\frac52}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q05"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_m21_qp_12.pdf`, Q2, and matching `9709_m21_ms_12.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q06}
### Question 6 · 9709/12/F/M/21 Q4

A line has equation (y=3x+k) and a curve has equation (y=x^2+kx+6), where (k) is a constant.

Find the set of values of (k) for which the line and curve have two distinct points of intersection. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

At an intersection,

$$x^2+kx+6=3x+k,$$

so

$$x^2+(k-3)x+(6-k)=0.$$

For two distinct intersections,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta&=(k-3)^2-4(6-k)>0\\
&=k^2-2k-15>0\\
&=(k-5)(k+3)>0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$\boxed{k<-3\text{ or }k>5}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q06"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_m21_qp_12.pdf`, Q4, and matching `9709_m21_ms_12.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q07}
### Question 7 · 9709/13/M/J/21 Q3

A line with equation (y=mx-6) is a tangent to the curve with equation (y=x^2-4x+3).

Find the possible values of the constant (m), and the corresponding coordinates of the points at which the line touches the curve. **[6]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

At a point of contact,

$$x^2-4x+3=mx-6,$$

so

$$x^2-(m+4)x+9=0.$$

For tangency,

$$
(m+4)^2-4(1)(9)=0.
$$

Thus (m+4=\pm6), giving

$$m=2\quad\text{or}\quad m=-10.
$$

The repeated root is (x=(m+4)/2). For (m=2), (x=3) and (y=2(3)-6=0), giving ((3,0)). For (m=-10), (x=-3) and (y=-10(-3)-6=24), giving ((-3,24)).

$$\boxed{(m,x,y)=(2,3,0)\text{ or }(-10,-3,24)}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q07"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_13.pdf`, Q3, and matching `9709_s21_ms_13.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q08}
### Question 8 · 9709/11/M/J/21 Q6

The equation of a curve is (y=(2k-3)x^2-kx-(k-2)), where (k) is a constant. The line (y=3x-4) is a tangent to the curve.

Find the value of (k). **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Equating the curve and the line,

$$
(2k-3)x^2-kx-(k-2)=3x-4,
$$

so

$$
(2k-3)x^2-(k+3)x-(k-6)=0.
$$

Tangency requires the discriminant to be zero:

$$
(k+3)^2+4(2k-3)(k-6)=0.
$$

Expanding,

$$k^2+6k+9+8k^2-60k+72=0,$$

so

$$9k^2-54k+81=9(k-3)^2=0.
$$

Therefore (oxed{k=3}).
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q08"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_11.pdf`, Q6, and matching `9709_s21_ms_11.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q09}
### Question 9 · 9709/12/F/M/22 Q2

A curve has equation (y=x^2+2cx+4) and a straight line has equation (y=4x+c), where (c) is a constant.

Find the set of values of (c) for which the curve and line intersect at two distinct points. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Equating the two equations,

$$x^2+2cx+4=4x+c,$$

so

$$x^2+(2c-4)x+(4-c)=0.$$

For two distinct intersections,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta&=(2c-4)^2-4(4-c)>0\\
&=4c^2-12c\\
&=4c(c-3)>0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Hence

$$\boxed{c<0\text{ or }c>3}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q09"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_m22_qp_12.pdf`, Q2, and matching `9709_m22_ms_12.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q10}
### Question 10 · 9709/12/F/M/22 Q5(a–b)

(a) Express (2x^2-8x+14) in the form (2(x-a)^2+b). **[2]**

The functions (f) and (g) are defined by (f(x)=x^2) and (g(x)=2x^2-8x+14), for (x\in\mathbb R).

(b) Describe fully a sequence of transformations that maps the graph of (y=f(x)) onto the graph of (y=g(x)), making clear the order in which the transformations are applied. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a)

$$
2x^2-8x+14=2(x^2-4x+4)+6=2(x-2)^2+6.
$$

So (a=2), (b=6).

(b) Starting from (y=x^2), first apply a stretch parallel to the (y)-axis with scale factor 2:

$$y=2x^2.
$$

Then translate 2 units to the right and 6 units upwards:

$$y=2(x-2)^2+6.
$$

Thus the required sequence is (oxed{\text{vertical stretch factor }2,\text{ followed by translation }(2,6)}).
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q10"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_m22_qp_12.pdf`, Q5(a–b), and matching `9709_m22_ms_12.pdf`.</div>
:::

### Question 11 · 9709/12/O/N/22 Q3(a–b)

(a) Find the set of values of (k) for which the equation (8x^2+kx+2=0) has no real roots. **[2]**

(b) Solve the equation (8\cos^2\theta-10\cos\theta+2=0) for (0^\circ\le\theta\le180^\circ). **[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a) No real roots means (Delta<0):

$$k^2-4(8)(2)<0\Longleftrightarrow k^2-64<0.$$

Therefore (oxed{-8<k<8}).

(b) Let (u=\cos\theta). Then

$$8u^2-10u+2=0\Longleftrightarrow 4u^2-5u+1=0,$$

so

$$
(4u-1)(u-1)=0.
$$

Hence (\cos\theta=\frac14) or (\cos\theta=1). In the stated interval,

$$\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac14\right)=75.5^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad\theta=0^\circ.
$$

Thus (oxed{\theta=0^\circ,\ 75.5^\circ}) (to 1 decimal place for the non-exact angle).
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q11"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_w22_qp_12.pdf`, Q3(a–b), and matching `9709_w22_ms_12.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q12}
### Question 12 · 9709/11/M/J/22 Q1(a–b)

(a) Express (x^2-8x+11) in the form ((x+p)^2+q), where (p) and (q) are constants. **[2]**

(b) Hence find the exact solutions of the equation (x^2-8x+11=1). **[2]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a)

$$x^2-8x+11=x^2-8x+16-5=(x-4)^2-5.$$

Thus (p=-4), (q=-5).

(b)

$$
(x-4)^2-5=1
\Longrightarrow (x-4)^2=6.
$$

Therefore

$$\boxed{x=4\pm\sqrt6}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q12"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_s22_qp_11.pdf`, Q1(a–b), and matching `9709_s22_ms_11.pdf`.</div>

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q13}
### Question 13 · 9709/12/F/M/23 Q1

A line has equation (y=3x-2k) and a curve has equation (y=x^2-kx+2), where (k) is a constant.

Show that the line and the curve meet for all values of (k). **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

At an intersection,

$$x^2-kx+2=3x-2k,$$

so

$$x^2-(k+3)x+(2+2k)=0.$$

Its discriminant is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta&=(k+3)^2-4(2+2k)\\
&=k^2-2k+1\\
&=(k-1)^2\ge0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus there are real values of (x) for every real (k), so the line and curve meet for all values of (k). When (k=1), (Delta=0) and the intersection is a repeated point; for all other (k), (Delta>0).
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q13"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_m23_qp_12.pdf`, Q1, and matching `9709_m23_ms_12.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q14}
### Question 14 · 9709/12/F/M/23 Q4

Solve the equation

$$8x^6+215x^3-27=0.$$

**[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Let (u=x^3). Then

$$8u^2+215u-27=0.$$

The discriminant is (215^2+4(8)(27)=217^2), so

$$
u=\frac{-215\pm217}{16}.
$$

Hence (u=\frac18) or (u=-27). Returning to (x),

$$x^3=\frac18\Longrightarrow x=\frac12,
\qquad x^3=-27\Longrightarrow x=-3.
$$

Therefore (oxed{x=\frac12\text{ or }x=-3}).
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q14"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_m23_qp_12.pdf`, Q4, and matching `9709_m23_ms_12.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q15}
### Question 15 · 9709/12/M/J/23 Q3(a–b)

(a) Express (4x^2-24x+p) in the form (a(x+b)^2+c), where (a) and (b) are integers and (c) is to be given in terms of the constant (p). **[2]**

(b) Hence or otherwise find the set of values of (p) for which the equation (4x^2-24x+p=0) has no real roots. **[1]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a)

$$
4x^2-24x+p=4(x^2-6x+9)+p-36=4(x-3)^2+p-36.
$$

Thus (a=4), (b=-3), (c=p-36).

(b) Since (4(x-3)^2\ge0), the minimum value of the quadratic is (p-36). For no real roots, this minimum must be positive:

$$p-36>0.
$$

Therefore (oxed{p>36}).
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q15"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_12.pdf`, Q3(a–b), and matching `9709_s23_ms_12.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q16}
### Question 16 · 9709/12/O/N/23 Q6(a–c)

The equation of a curve is (y=x^2-8x+5).

(a) Find the coordinates of the minimum point of the curve. **[2]**

The curve is stretched by a factor of 2 parallel to the (y)-axis and then translated by

$$\begin{pmatrix}4\\1\end{pmatrix}.$$

(b) Find the coordinates of the minimum point of the transformed curve. **[2]**

(c) Find the equation of the transformed curve. Give the answer in the form (y=ax^2+bx+c), where (a), (b) and (c) are integers to be found. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a)

$$y=x^2-8x+5=(x-4)^2-11,$$

so the minimum point is (oxed{(4,-11)}).

(b) A vertical stretch by factor 2 sends the minimum value (-11) to (-22). The subsequent translation by ((4,1)) sends the vertex ((4,-22)) to

$$\boxed{(8,-21)}.$$

(c) After the vertical stretch,

$$y=2(x-4)^2-22.
$$

Translating by ((4,1)) replaces (x) by (x-4) and adds 1 to (y):

$$
y=2((x-4)-4)^2-22+1=2(x-8)^2-21.
$$

Expanding,

$$\boxed{y=2x^2-32x+107}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q16"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_12.pdf`, Q6(a–c), and matching `9709_w23_ms_12.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q17}
### Question 17 · 9709/11/M/J/24 Q1(a–b)

(a) Express (3y^2-12y-15) in the form (3(y+a)^2+b), where (a) and (b) are constants. **[2]**

(b) Hence find the exact solutions of the equation (3x^4-12x^2-15=0). **[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a)

$$
3y^2-12y-15=3(y^2-4y-5)=3\bigl((y-2)^2-9\bigr),
$$

so

$$\boxed{3y^2-12y-15=3(y-2)^2-27}.
$$

Thus (a=-2), (b=-27).

(b) Put (y=x^2) in the completed-square result:

$$
3(x^2-2)^2-27=0
\Longrightarrow (x^2-2)^2=9.
$$

Therefore (x^2-2=\pm3). This gives (x^2=5) or (x^2=-1). Only the first gives real solutions, so

$$\boxed{x=\pm\sqrt5}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-quad-q17"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> `PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p11.pdf`, Q1(a–b), and matching `ms-202406-mathematics-p11.pdf`.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q18}
### Question 18 · 9709/13/M/J/24 Q11

The function (f) is defined by

$$f(x)=10+6x-x^2\quad\text{for }x\in\mathbb R.$$

By completing the square, find the range of (f). **[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

$$
f(x)=10+6x-x^2=-(x^2-6x-10)
=-(x-3)^2+19.
$$

Since (-(x-3)^2\le0), the greatest value of (f) is 19, attained at (x=3). As (x\to\pm\infty), (f(x)\to-\infty). Hence

$$\boxed{\text{range of }f=(-\infty,19]}.$$
</details>

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q19}
### Question 19 · 9709/11/O/N/24 Q11(a)

The function (f) is defined by

$$f(x)=3+6x-2x^2\quad\text{for }x\in\mathbb R.$$

Express (f(x)) in the form (a-b(x-c)^2), where (a), (b) and (c) are constants, and state the range of (f). **[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

$$
f(x)=3+6x-2x^2=-2(x^2-3x)+3
$$

$$
=-2\left((x-\tfrac32)^2-\tfrac94\right)+3
=-2\left(x-\tfrac32\right)^2+\frac{15}{2}.
$$

Thus (a=\frac{15}{2}), (b=2), (c=\frac32). The maximum value is (\frac{15}{2}), and the quadratic decreases without bound, so

$$\boxed{\text{range of }f=(-\infty,\tfrac{15}{2}]}.$$
</details>

:::

::: {.question-card #p1-quad-q20}
### Question 20 · 9709/12/O/N/24 Q7(a)

By expressing (-2x^2+8x+11) in the form (-a(x-b)^2+c), where (a), (b) and (c) are positive integers, find the coordinates of the vertex of the graph with equation (y=-2x^2+8x+11). **[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=-2(x^2-4x)+11\\
&=-2\bigl((x-2)^2-4\bigr)+11\\
&=-2(x-2)^2+19.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus (a=2), (b=2), (c=19). Since the coefficient of the square is negative, the graph has a maximum (its vertex) at

$$\boxed{(2,19)}.$$
</details>
